statement: The function returns a result r. If the value sequence of r is [r_0,...,r_{L-1}], then L=m and r_j=S_j for every j with 0<=j<m. Thus r is exactly the list of sums of the nonempty blocks of input values lying strictly between consecutive zero-valued nodes.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the value sequence of head, so head=Cons(x_0,Cons(x_1,...Cons(x_{n-1},Nil))). Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n, x_0=0, x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent values are both 0. Let z_0<z_1<...<z_m be all indices i with x_i=0; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2 for every 0<=j<m. For 0<=j<m define S_j=sum_{i=z_j+1}^{z_{j+1}-1} x_i.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, the number of nodes in r is len(r)=m, which is one less than the number of zero-valued nodes in head. Equivalently, r has exactly one node for each nonempty block of input values between two consecutive zero-valued nodes.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, every value in r is positive: for every i with 0<=i<len(r), the i-th value of r is at least 1. In particular, r contains no node whose value is 0.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, for every j with 0<=j<m, the j-th value of r exists and satisfies 1 <= value_j(r) <= 1000*(z_{j+1}-z_j-1).
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2. For 0<=j<m define S_j=sum_{i=z_j+1}^{z_{j+1}-1} x_i.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, the sum of all node values in r equals the sum of all node values in head: sum_{i=0}^{len(r)-1} value_i(r) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i. Since every zero-valued input node contributes 0, this is also the sum of all nonzero input values.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, its length satisfies 1 <= len(r) <= floor((n-1)/2).
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r and m=1 (equivalently, the only zero-valued nodes are the first and last nodes), r has exactly one node and its only value is sum_{i=1}^{n-2} x_i.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r and z_{j+1}=z_j+2 for every 0<=j<m (equivalently n=2m+1 and every block between consecutive zeros consists of exactly one node), then for every 0<=j<m the j-th value of r is x_{2j+1}.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, len(r)=m; for every output index j with 0<=j<m, the j-th value of r is S_j, so the witness interval for output j is (z_j,z_{j+1}); and every input index i with x_i != 0 lies in exactly one interval (z_k,z_{k+1}) with 0<=k<m.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2. For 0<=j<m define S_j=sum_{i=z_j+1}^{z_{j+1}-1} x_i.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, merge_nodes head returns a result r; it does not fail by panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow. In particular every segment sum S_j satisfies S_j <= 1000*200000 = 200000000, which is far below the maximum i64 value, so forming all sums is safe.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2. For 0<=j<m define S_j=sum_{i=z_j+1}^{z_{j+1}-1} x_i.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, the first value of r (index 0) equals sum_{i=1}^{z_1-1} x_i, the sum of the initial nonzero run immediately after the first zero and before the next zero.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, the last value of r (index len(r)-1) equals sum_{i=z_{m-1}+1}^{n-2} x_i, the sum of the final nonzero run after the penultimate zero and before the final zero.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, len(r)=m, and for all j,k with 0<=j<k<m, every input index i with z_j < i < z_{j+1} is less than every input index i' with z_k < i' < z_{k+1}.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0. Let z_0<...<z_m be the zero indices; then z_0=0, z_m=n-1, m>=1, and z_{j+1}>=z_j+2.

statement: Whenever merge_nodes head returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of maximal contiguous runs of indices i with x_i != 0 in the input value sequence xs.
preconditions: Let xs=[x_0,...,x_{n-1}] be the values of head. Assume 3<=n<=200000, 0<=x_i<=1000 for all i, x_0=x_{n-1}=0, and no two adjacent x_i are both 0.
